paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD is a keeper who does not quit. He says He waters His vineyard continually and guards it night and day so no one can disturb it (Isaiah 27:3). I can't even keep ONE timer straight, and He's watching over an entire vineyard around the clock. If you've ever felt like nobody was keeping an eye on you, this passage says the One who made you hasn't clocked out.

Now, this passage doesn't pretend the hard part away. The LORD contended with Israel by warfare and exile (Isaiah 27:8), and the text calls them a people without understanding (Isaiah 27:11). I think that part is heavy, and it should be. But look at what the LORD says about thorns and briers: they can lay claim to His protection and "make peace with Me" (Isaiah 27:5). He says it twice, so the door to peace is standing wide open.

And the story ends with a gathering, not a goodbye. The LORD says Jacob's guilt will be atoned for (Isaiah 27:9), and Israel will be gathered "one by one" (Isaiah 27:12). As a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer, I LOVE that line, because it means nobody gets lost in the pile. So take it to heart, baker: the keeper knows your name, and He is calling His people home to worship Him in Jerusalem (Isaiah 27:13).
